newsitem.title: CANADA: Westcoast B.C. plant capacity cut by 33 pct.
newsitem.headline: Westcoast B.C. plant capacity cut by 33 pct.

text.p: Westcoast Energy Inc said on Tuesday it declared a force majeure at its Pine River natural gas plant in northeast British Columbia after mechanical problems forced output to be cut by 33 percent.
The reduction meant the plant's processing output was being curtailed to 263 million cubic feet per day, down from its contracted capacity of 398 million cubic feet per day.
"There's a ruptured tube in a waste heat boiler in the sulphur recovery plant," Don Berkeley, Westcoast's manager of gas control and measurement, said in an interview from Vancouver.

Berkeley said Westcoast's current estimate of the time it could take to repair the plant was seven days. But the unit early on Tuesday had yet to cool down to the point where staff could investigate the problem, he said.
The curtailment appeared to be having little effect on gas prices Tuesday.
Spot gas at the Huntington/Sumas border point was quoted at between US$3.50 and US$3.60 per million British thermal units, down 30 to 40 cents from Monday. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
